attributes.title: Level 5

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using different combinations of symbols in your code to assign and check the value of variables.

questions.hint: What symbol assigns a value to a variable in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] What symbol should be used in the blank space to assign an initial value to the variable?
questions.correctResponse: An assignment operator (=) is used so that the computerX variable is assigned an initial value of 10.

questions.hint: What does a single equal sign do in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] A single equal sign in JavaScript works the same way as the equal sign does in the equation 2 + 2 = 4.
questions.correctResponse: An assignment operator (=) works differently than an equal sign in a math operation; it doesn’t mean “equal to”. Instead, it assigns the variable on the left of the operator an initial value to the right of the operator.

questions.hint: How is the == symbol used in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] What is this operator called and how does it work in the code?

answers.text: Equality operator. This symbol checks if the variable named on the left of the operator is equal to the value named on the right.
Assignment operator. The variable on the left of the operator is assigned an initial value to the right of the operator.
Inequality operator. This symbol checks if the variable named on the left of the operator is not equal to the value named on the right.
Addition operator. This operator takes the variable’s value, then adds the value named on the right of the operator. The variable is assigned the updated value.

questions.correctResponse: In JavaScript, == represents an equality operator. It can be used to check if the value of the variable on the left of the operator is equal to the value on the right.

questions.hint: What else will happen  to the chocCookieY and chocCookieStack variables when the A button is pressed?
questions.title: [Select all that apply] What will happen to the chocCookieY and chocCookieStack variables when the A button is pressed? (Check all that apply)

answers.text: The value of chocCookieY will decrease by 2
The value of chocCookieY will be assigned to  2
The value of chocCookieStack will increase by 1
The value of chocCookieStack will be assigned to 1

questions.correctResponse: An addition assignment operator (+=) takes the variable’s value, then adds the value named on the right of the operator. The variable is assigned the updated value. A subtraction assignment operator (-=) subtracts the value named on the right of the operator from the variable’s original value. The variable is assigned the updated value.

steps.text: [Select one]  What will the dialog box say when it appears on the screen?

questions.hint: What do plus signs (+) placed between strings and variables do in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one]  What will the dialog box say when it appears on the screen?
questions.correctResponse: In JavaScript, plus signs (+) are used to join, or concatenate, strings and variables. The variable’s value is then inserted into the dialog box message!

subgroups.title: Assignment and Equality Operators!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using different combinations of symbols in your code to assign and check the value of variables.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about assignment and equality operators, which can be used to assign, change, and check for a variable’s value. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: One Equals Sign or Two?
badges.description: Use the correct symbols to create assignment and equality operators to assign, change, and check for a variable’s value in JavaScript.

badges.title: Let There Be Variables
badges.description: Create a variable using let in JavaScript.

badges.title: Concatenation Station
badges.description: Concatenate two or more strings together using the + operator.

badges.title: Asset Depreciation
badges.description: Use the subtraction assignment operator to decrease the value of a number variable.

badges.title: Incremental Growth
badges.description: Use the addition assignment operator to increase the value of a number variable.

badges.title: I’m Thinking of a Number
badges.description: Use the askForNumber function to assign a user-inputted value to a variable.

badges.title: It’s Back on the Menu
badges.description: Write code that runs when the Menu button is pressed.
